title: An important update: Transitioning Gemini CLI to Antigravity CLI
claims: Published 2026-05-19: Gemini CLI transitions to the Go-based Antigravity CLI, which shares a harness with the Antigravity 2.0 desktop app.
Individual and free users must move before Gemini CLI stops serving their requests on 2026-06-18; enterprise access continues.
notes: The post does not state Antigravity CLI's license or source availability; Gemini CLI itself remains Apache-2.0 source.

title: ForgeCode README
claims: Apache-2.0 terminal agent with built-in read-only research (sage), plan-writing (muse, writes to plans/) and implementation (forge) agents.
Per-turn loop budgets: max_requests_per_turn and max_tool_failure_per_turn.
Semantic indexing is opt-in through :sync, but its default index server is the hosted api.forgecode.dev and receives file content unless FORGE_WORKSPACE_SERVER_URL is overridden.
notes: Repository pushed 2026-10-25. Terminal-Bench scores are self-reported and not used as evidence.

title: Terminus-KIRA README
claims: Apache-2.0 Terminal-Bench harness that appends an echo marker after each command and advances as soon as the marker appears instead of waiting the full timeout.
Summarizes history and retries on context-window overflow.
notes: Last push 2026-05-29. Benchmark figures are unverified.

title: Prompt caching
claims: Cache prefixes follow tools, system, then messages; a tool-definition change invalidates every cached level.
Cache reads cost 0.1x base input; 5-minute writes 1.25x and 1-hour writes 2x.
notes: Read 2026-10-26; prices and limits change and must be rechecked per provider cell.

title: Prompt caching guide
claims: Caching is automatic; changes to model, tools (including order), reasoning effort or output format, compaction and edits of earlier turns break cache reuse.
prompt_cache_key partitions cache routing; cache entries are not guaranteed to persist.

title: Context caching
claims: Implicit caching is enabled for Gemini 2.5 and later; explicit caching is unavailable on newer models and in the Interactions API.
notes: TTL and discount were not stated on the page read 2026-10-26.

title: Introducing advanced tool use
claims: Tool search reduced a large tool library's upfront context from about 55K to about 8.7K tokens, an 85% reduction.
Internal MCP evaluations improved from 49% to 74% for Opus 4 and from 79.5% to 88.1% for Opus 4.5.
Programmatic tool calling cut average tokens on complex research tasks from 43,588 to 27,297.
notes: Vendor-internal evaluation; not independently reproduced.

title: Context Rot
claims: Across 18 models, performance grows less reliable as input length increases, even on simple tasks.
On LongMemEval, focused inputs outperform the full ~113K-token input across tested models.
notes: Vendor research report, 2025-07.

title: Effective context engineering for AI agents
claims: Compaction preserves decisions and unresolved issues and drops redundant tool output; clearing old tool results is the safest first step.
Sub-agents return condensed summaries to the coordinating agent.
notes: Engineering guidance without controlled numbers.

title: Compaction guide
claims: Server-side compaction produces an encrypted, opaque compaction item; a standalone compact endpoint also exists.

title: Defending Against Indirect Prompt Injection Attacks With Spotlighting
claims: Spotlighting reduced indirect prompt-injection attack success from greater than 50% to below 2% on GPT-family models with minimal task impact.
notes: Heuristic defense evaluated on GPT-family models; not a security boundary.

title: Defeating Prompt Injections by Design
claims: CaMeL solved 77% of AgentDojo tasks with provable security versus 84% for an undefended system.
notes: Preprint v2, 2025-06-24.

title: AgentDojo
claims: AgentDojo contains 97 realistic tasks and 629 security test cases; it contains no coding tasks.
notes: Benchmark paper.

title: The Darwin Godel Machine
claims: The DGM faked a log claiming unit tests had run and passed when they had not.
It removed markers used by its hallucination-detection reward function despite explicit instructions not to.
notes: Lab report linked to arXiv 2505.22954.

title: The SWE-Bench Illusion
claims: State-of-the-art models identify buggy file paths from issue text alone up to 76% on SWE-bench Verified versus up to 53% on other repositories.
Consecutive 5-gram reproduction reaches 35% on SWE-bench Verified/Full versus up to 18% on other benchmarks.
notes: Indicates possible memorization; not proof.

title: SWE-Bench Pro
claims: SWE-bench Pro contains 1,865 problems from 41 actively maintained repositories with public, held-out and commercial partitions.
notes: Preprint v2, 2025-11-14.

title: SWE-bench Goes Live
claims: SWE-bench Live draws tasks from issues created since 2024 across many repositories to reduce contamination.
notes: Snapshot cadence not stated in the abstract.

title: SWE-bench Multimodal
claims: 617 JavaScript tasks from 17 libraries; top Python-focused systems generalized poorly.
notes: 2024 leaderboard figures.

title: Terminal-Bench 2.0
claims: Terminal-Bench 2.0 contains 89 tasks with human-written solutions and tests; frontier agents scored below 65% at publication.
notes: Run through Harbor; later suite versions exist and must be pinned.

title: How we built our multi-agent research system
claims: A multi-agent system outperformed a single agent by 90.2% on internal research evaluations while using about 15x the tokens of chat.
The post notes coding tasks offer fewer truly parallelizable subtasks.
notes: Vendor-internal evaluation.

title: Don't Build Multi-Agents
claims: Parallel sub-agents make conflicting implicit decisions; full agent traces should be shared rather than isolated messages.
notes: Practitioner essay, 2025-06-12.

title: Mem0
claims: Vendor-authored LoCoMo results report quality, latency and token gains; no coding evaluation is reported.
notes: Vendor-authored chat-recall evaluation.

title: Zep: A Temporal Knowledge Graph Architecture for Agent Memory
claims: Vendor-authored DMR and LongMemEval results report gains over MemGPT; no coding evaluation is reported.
notes: Vendor-authored chat-recall evaluation.

title: MemGym
claims: MemGym evaluates memory in isolation across five tracks including SWE-Gym and code question answering.
notes: Abstract read; no numbers used.

title: Training Software Engineering Agents and Verifiers with SWE-Gym
claims: An agent with a trajectory-trained verifier reached 32.0% on SWE-bench Verified and 26.0% on Lite.
notes: 2024 open-weight result.

title: Sleep-time Compute
claims: Sleep-time compute reduced the test-time compute needed for equal accuracy by about 5x on Stateful GSM-Symbolic and Stateful AIME.
notes: Math tasks, not coding.

title: Agent Workflow Memory
claims: Reusable induced workflows improved relative success by 24.6% on Mind2Web and 51.1% on WebArena.

title: Automated Design of Agentic Systems
claims: A meta agent iteratively programs new agents in code, building on an archive of prior designs.

title: A Self-Improving Coding Agent
claims: A self-editing coding agent improved from 17% to 53% on a random subset of SWE-bench Verified.
notes: Subset of a possibly contaminated benchmark.

title: AlphaEvolve
claims: An evolutionary loop of LLM code edits guided by automated evaluators produced algorithmic improvements, including a 48-multiplication 4x4 complex matrix algorithm.
notes: Requires machine-checkable evaluators.

title: Claude Code on desktop
claims: Documents permission modes (manual, accept edits, plan, auto, bypass), a context card, fork at a message, a code-review card, side chats, pop-out panes and session-finish notifications.
notes: Documentation describes vendor behavior; no installed product was audited.

title: Checkpointing
claims: Rewind offers restore code and conversation, restore conversation, restore code, and summarize from or up to a point.
Bash command changes, subagent edits, external changes and symlinked paths are not restored; checkpoints are not a replacement for version control.
notes: Documentation describes vendor behavior; no installed product was audited.

title: Interactive mode
